items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-09-08
items.q: I know a fellow named Duffy. And that fellow stood sick for three years.

ctx.x: Well, the clubs and the societies the same, or are there differences between them, or what?

Well, I think Balevalin is, they put you on the same basis. I tell you the reason why I say they're on the same basis. They give you, some give you a doctor in medicine, in the barrel, you know. Then a club, they might give you a, they'll bury it, they might give you a little sick, that's bad, they don't furnish you to no doctor, you see. They might furnish you medicine or something like that. But a man do better blocking the club than doing society. You see, because society don't do like a club do. A club can…
I was just going to ask if you think more people today belong to insurance or to clubs. I mean, do you think?
